utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Tuesday, April 8, 2008, and I welcome the representatives from the OTP, Mr. Seselj, as well as all the people helping us. In the meanwhile, the problem has cropped up. Witness VS-031, who was scheduled to testify today, and I will not give his name because he was a protected witness, well, this person told the OTP, by fax on Friday, April 4th, at 8.47 that he decided to be a Defence witness after all, and because of this the OTP was not able to get Witness VS-031 in time here. Furthermore, Witness VS-1014 is scheduled to come, but he was unable to be here today because of a visa problem. However, I believe that this person will be here tomorrow, at the latest. Witness VS-1062, who is scheduled to come, will come, but it was impossible to get him here today. Because of this, the Prosecution has decided to continue with the videos, the videos which we have already seen last week, but we did not finish the entire list of videos last week. Furthermore, I also understood the Prosecution wanted to add new videos to its list. As soon as I was informed of this, I asked the legal officer yesterday to immediately tell Mr. Seselj about this, about the possibility that there may be new videos. The legal officer ran into terrible difficulties trying to transfer this information to the UNDU. She had to stay until 9.30 p.m. to try to get the information through. So this is proof that, as I say, this Trial Chamber is doing its utmost around the clock to make sure everything runs smoothly. Unfortunately, despite all our efforts, sometimes there are difficulties, and because of this some problems escape unsolved, at least can't be solved in realtime, which means, Mr. Seselj, that today we will be watching the rest of the videos, the videos which had been scheduled last week, plus - but Mr. Mundis must confirm this to us - new videos, new videos, and you must have received the list of these videos. Maybe so, maybe not. Mr. Mundis, regarding the videos, will we see new videos also?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good, Your Honours, Dr. Seselj, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Unfortunately, we will not be showing any additional videos this morning, due to the fact that we are undertaking a review to determine the precise videos that absolutely must be shown, and as a result of that we determined that it would be best for us to come up with a priority "A" list of videos, and we were not able to sort through all of those videos in the time that was available to us. So we will simply be showing those videos which were previously listed and for which everyone in the courtroom has sufficient notice that those videos would be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well. I was talking about difficulties. Here we have one. The light goes on, the light goes out, but fortunately the light is back on. Now, let's go into private session, because I have something that requires private session, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, first I wish to express my standpoint on some issues you have already raised, Mr. President. Yesterday, in the prison, I was not informed of your intention to show new video clips today. Yesterday, our floor moved, so maybe they couldn't find us at our new address, because there's some kind of construction work going on there. However, that's not a problem. I could adapt to these surprising announcements that new video clips are going to be shown. I don't prepare for these videos because I don't have a DVD projector in my prison cell, so there's no way I can prepare. I'm always prepared to have videos shown in the courtroom, even if not announced, as long as I'm provided with a list of these clips in the Serbian language. I have to tell you, however, that I never previously contacted Protected Witness VS-031. He contacted my legal advisers for the first time on Friday. He personally sought them out, with his lawyer, and on that occasion he made a statement to them. I haven't received it yet. I can obtain it in the course of today. But in that statement, he said, among other things, that he was disgusted by the acquittal of Ramos Haradinaj, and he refuses to cooperate with The Hague Prosecutor in any way. He has put himself at the disposal of my Defence team, but we'll consider whether or not to call him as a Defence witness. I just wish you to know that we never had any previous contact with him. A third point, very important, in my view, is that I demand that you re-examine your decision to admit 92 ter witness statements, especially in the case of Witness VS-1014. This witness I consider to be a very important one, and I have some important questions to put to him. But I will only do so if he testifies viva voce. I therefore propose that the OTP has one and a half hours at their disposal and I one and a half hours, one hour of reserve for questions from the Trial Chambers and procedural issues, and we will be able to deal with that witness in one day. I have important questions to put to that witness, but unless you agree to my proposal, I will certainly not put them. And, fourthly, yesterday I received from the OTP a document entitled "Receipt 309." This was delivered to me as a public document, so I will mention a name contained in it. The OTP disclosed to me a letter from a certain Dusan Damjanovic from Kragujevac. I have never heard of him before. This letter bears number 06328586, so I assume it can be provided in electronic form on the monitor and that you will be able to see it before you, if the Registry makes this possible. This Dusan Damjanovic, and let me mention that he was never mentioned as an OTP witness in this case and no document I received bore his name, nor was he mentioned, to the best of my recollection, in any of the documents. However, here he's informing the OTP in The Hague that he doesn't wish to be a Prosecution witness in the proceedings against me, and he says that Natasha Kandic called him up more than once with her collaborators in order for him to be interviewed by investigators. So he wants to know in what capacity Natasha Kandic is calling him up or, rather, his lawyer is asking this, in what capacity she's calling him up, attempting to persuade him to be interviewed by the OTP. I did not know that this man existed until last night. I had never contacted him. And although the investigation is over and the OTP list is complete, some names are still cropping up. Natasha Kandic is attempting to exert pressure on certain people still, so the OTP should tell us in what capacity Natasha Kandic is acting. Is she an official representative of the OTP or is she some sort of external associate? She's eminence grise in The Hague OTP. I don't know about this man. I don't know what he might testify about. I had never heard his name before. But now my legal advisers are going to contact him, and we will see who he is and what this is all about. He may be useful as a Defence witness, but I can't say that in advance. However, I'm duty-bound to inform you that such things are happening here and nobody is providing any kind of explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Two things, Mr. Seselj, and I will deal with them in reverse order. First, Dusan Damjanovic, if I understand you well, this witness, who is not on the 65 ter list, contacted your associates to tell them --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me correct you, Mr. President. He has not contacted my collaborators yet. He has sent a letter to the OTP, and last night the OTP delivered to me a copy of the letter with its ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are right to correct this. So this Dusan Damjanovic, who you do not know and whom you have never heard of before, sent a letter to the OTP to say that Natasha Kandic had approached him so that he would testify, and he is saying that he would rather be in favour of being a Defence witness, rather than a Prosecution witness. Mr. Mundis, does this mean that you are continuing the investigation and collecting testimonies from potential witnesses in order to possibly ask for -- possibly call some witnesses? Is this the framework in which we have this witness, which seemed to be unknown by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the event, the Prosecution would seek leave to amend its witness list, I can assure everyone that we would do so in a timely manner. This person, Mr. Dusan Damjanovic was, to the best of my knowledge, unknown to the Prosecution prior to him sending this faxed letter. I don't believe at this point we're even close to potentially calling this person as a witness. I don't believe we've ever interviewed him. We've never spoken to him. The Office of the Prosecutor gets faxes and correspondence and information on a daily basis from a large number of sources, not just relating to this case but to all of our cases. When we determine that that information should be disclosed, we disclose it. But at this point, it's entirely premature to be discussing whether or not this person will be a witness for the Prosecution, or the Defence, or for anyone else. He simply sent us a letter, and we determined that that needed to be disclosed to the accused. And that's as far as this issue has been taken. And so it's certainly not at the point where we're contemplating seeking leave to add Mr. Damjanovic to the witness list. We've never even spoken to this person, to the best of my knowledge, and so it's entirely premature at this point to be discussing anything relating to this witness or potential witness as it relates to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The second thing, Witness VS-1014. Let me remind you that on February 27th, the Trial Chamber decided -- made a decision according to which this witness would be heard as a 92 ter witness. Since then, no certification of appeal has been filed. Of course, if need be, the Chamber can review its decision in light of two criteria. The first criterion, a new circumstance. And what is this new circumstance which would lead the Trial Chamber to review its decision? And a second criterion, err in law, the Trial Chamber could be made an error, could have erred in law. Now, Mr. Seselj, regarding this first circumstance, the first criterion. What would be the new circumstance that would lead the Chamber to decide to switch to a viva voce procedure with one hour thirty for Prosecution and one hour thirty minutes for Defence? Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have decided not to appeal your latest decision because I have expressed my objections to the application of Rule 92 ter more than once. So I don't want my legal advisers and you to waste time about this. I know that my appeal would be rejected. I am concentrating on this witness, who is supposed to appear tomorrow. A new circumstance which might be relevant to your decision and induce you to change it is that his statement about certain events, given to the Muslim authorities, differs considerably to the statement compiled in his name by the OTP and signed by him. These two statements are so different from each other that it would be quite incredible for you to turn a deaf ear to my motion. However, that's up to you. I have some very important specific questions, concrete questions, to put to that witness, but they are not important enough for you to alter your decision. You can look at his statement given before the Muslim authorities and the statement disclosed by the OTP, and you will see to what extent the two statements differ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let me ask the Prosecution about these new circumstances. It is true that when the Trial Chamber made its decision on December 27th, 2008 [as interpreted], we did not know that a statement had been made to the Muslim authorities. This emerged just a few days ago when another witness said that he had been heard by the Muslim authorities. We knew nothing of this. What is the position of the OTP regarding the possibility of switching this 92 ter into a viva voce witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is absolutely no new circumstance whatsoever, other than the fact that Dr. Seselj has now decided that perhaps he would like to cross-examine the witness. Your Honours are well aware of the position taken by the accused in this case with respect to Rule 92 ter. As a matter of fact, just last week the Presiding Judge, in effect, advised the accused that perhaps he should reconsider his decision. There is absolutely no reason or justification whatsoever for the Trial Chamber to reconsider its decision. The accused always will have the opportunity, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, to cross-examine the witness. The witness will be brought here. The witness can be challenged with any previous statements that he may or may not have given. He can be fully cross-examined as to that statement or statements. What the Prosecution would certainly oppose would be any situation where the accused declines to cross-examine the witness and then subsequently sought to tender into evidence a prior statement of that witness which the accused thought would be inconsistent having had the opportunity to cross-examine the witness on that point and then having decided not to do so. There is absolutely no bar to the accused cross-examining this 92 ter witness or any other 92 ter witness. This procedure, as the Trial Chamber is well aware, is designed to expedite the proceedings. The Prosecution, in its pre-trial filings, had indicated preference for a large number of Rule 92 ter witness in order to put before the Trial Chamber all of the evidence which the Trial Chamber will require in order to fulfill its obligations with respect to making final and ultimate decisions in this case. In the event the Prosecution is unable to rely upon Rule 92 ter, then we will certainly be coming back before the Trial Chamber asking for significantly longer time in order to lead the evidence that we feel is necessary in order to establish the charges set forth in the indictment. I cannot stress enough, Your Honours, the simple fact that the accused has decided not to cross-examine 92 ter witnesses. That's his choice. If he chooses not to do so, the responsibility for that falls squarely on his shoulders. The witness will be here. The witness can be cross-examined. There is absolutely no reason for the Trial Chamber to reconsider its decision simply because the accused decides he now wants to cross-examine the witness and he had earlier made a stand that he will not, as a matter of principle, cross-examine any of the 92 ter witnesses. So the Prosecution would vehemently oppose reconsideration of the Trial Chamber earlier decision concerning this witness, and we will again telegraph for the future that in the event we are unable to rely upon Rule 92 ter as a means of putting forth the evidence that we need in the limited time available to us, we will have no choice but to come back to the Trial Chamber and ask for significantly more time in order to lead the evidence that we feel duty-bound to lead so that the Trial Chamber has all of the evidence that it needs to reach the ultimate decisions that the Trial Chamber is called upon to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's come back to -- let's resume, because we had a technical problem. The Prosecution decides that there is no new circumstances. Now, Mr. Seselj, over the last three days I've tried to think about the stand you took, which was to systematically oppose Rule 92 ter. I tried to understand why you reject this procedure. It's quite complicated to try and anticipate why someone is doing something. I was thinking and I wondered whether maybe at first you were not making a mistake as to the admission of the written statement. Maybe you're thinking that the written statement will automatically be admitted if the Prosecutor asks for Rule 92 ter to be applied. But if this is what you're thinking, this is a mistake. The Trial Chamber will only rule on the admissibility of the written statement after the cross-examination of the witness. For example, if it suddenly appears that a written statement totally contradicts another statement that would have been made to another jurisdiction, well, in such a case the Trial Chamber could very well decide not to admit the written statement. The written statement will only be admitted after the cross-examination and after the Judges have heard the cross-examination. It's only after having assessed the entire procedure that the Judges will decide to admit the written statement or not to admit it. That's the first thing. The second thing: I also wondered whether, in reality, if you just didn't feel that you -- you felt that there was a deficit of information for the audience following the trial, because it's -- when there is a written statement, no questions are -- no specific questions are asked as to this written statement, only a few general questions are asked, and because of this part of the written statement would be hidden from the audience, whereas in a viva voce procedure you're assured that the trial is public and you're assured that the audience will hear everything the witness is saying. Of course, when there is a written statement, the witness just says, "I confirm what I said to the investigator," and then the cross-examination starts. So I wondered whether this was not one of your motivations, to reject this 92 ter -- the Rule 92 ter procedure, because I must say very humbly that as of now, I have not really fully understood the real motivations behind your opposition to this procedure. As I reminded you, you know, you can use this procedure yourself, you can resort to this procedure yourself, when you have a number of witnesses you want to call and when you don't have enough time to call all your witnesses to ask all your questions, you can resort to Rule 92 ter yourself. So this is where things stand now. If you wish to take the floor, you may, but I must tell you that the Bench does not really understand your position. We're a bit lost here. We don't really understand why you so vehemently oppose Rule 92 ter, especially since, as Mr. Mundis said, you have the opportunity to cross-examine this witness. Furthermore, when you have elements at your disposal that could contradict the written statement, according to the Rules you can confront the witness with this. This is Rule 98(ii). I will quote it in full so that it is on the record. Rule 90(H)(ii): "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel should put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." Which means that if you have this declaration, this statement to the Muslim authorities, and that in the procedure we have the written statement, well, you can resort to this Rule. But I believe my fellow Judge would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to add one thing to what the Presiding Judge just said. I understood Mr. Seselj's opposition to Rule 92 ter as follows: In principle, it is against -- he's against any trial based on documents, which is why also he is also presenting all sorts of documents when there is a witness, but never asks for these documents to be admitted. Therefore, this is, of course, as the Prosecutor has said -- I'm sorry, I don't know why I'm hearing the English. Can you speak in English now, please? I can't hear it anymore. I'm sorry, I had a problem, because I could hear both languages at the same time. So this is a question of principle. This Tribunal, for reasons that have been decided a year ago, maybe more than that - I don't remember - in order to speed up the trials and in the interests of the accused, the Trial Chamber has decided, as regards 92 ter, that this should be the case, so we, the Bench, cannot accept challenges as a matter of principle. I would like to add something to what the Presiding Judge has said; namely, this procedure -- to corroborate what he has said, this procedure does not mean that the prior statement of the witness is automatically admitted. This is why I don't see in what way the trial does not benefit from the fact that this is an oral -- that these are oral and public proceedings if Rule 92 ter is applied. The accused has all latitude and has even more than that, because he might even rely on those challenges to the prior statement rather than if the witness testifies viva voce, because when the witness testifies viva voce, he starts telling a story all over again, whereas if it's 92 ter, he can work and rely on the contradictions that stem from this. So as far as logic is concerned, I believe that the Trial Chamber should not bear this in mind and the accused can work on this and challenge it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with what my fellow Judge has said, something which might have escaped some people. We have realised that you never ask for documents to be admitted. You might do this at a later stage, but as my fellow Judge has just said, as far as you're concerned, you feel that the procedure should be a fully oral procedure, which would explain your position. In other words, you would not be in favour of any form of statement. Now, this is just on a personal note, Mr. Seselj. I must tell you that as far as I'm concerned, given that I have been in my job for the last 30 years and I've been involved in criminal law, a written document is always important, and sometimes it is even more important than what a witness can say when he comes and talks about events which occurred more than 20 years ago, and he may suffer from memory loss. However, a document that was drafted 20 years ago can be relied upon, unless of course it's a forged document. This is why it is extremely important to have documents. And if, as a matter of principle, you declare that you are only in favour of oral proceedings, well, this could handicap your own Defence because you might have crucial documents that you wish to have admitted in support of your case. In that case, those documents could be vital to you. This is a mixed -- these are mixed proceedings. It's a combination of civil law and common law proceedings, and this Tribunal is tending to admit more and more evidence that has already been admitted in other cases, or in favour of admitting material evidence that was collected through documents. Oral testimony is one thing, but oral testimony, when it is not corroborated by evidence, has less of a probative value. Oral testimony in addition to documents has a greater probative value. Would you like to say something again on this crucial issue, i.e., Rule 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll take these matters in reverse order as well. Firstly, as far as the issue raised by Judge Lattanzi, your colleague, is concerned, the issue on documents that I submit or do not submit. I have submitted documents to you. I suggested they be admitted into evidence, but you refused this request. I have tried to collect 160 documents through my associates, assistants. They concerned the Sarajevo battlefield, and these documents show that there were no volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party there at the relevant places and at the relevant times. So I'm talking about volunteers who were sent to the battlefield from Serbia. The Prosecution said that they don't bring this into question, but you refuse to admit this into evidence. Secondly, as far as Prosecution documents are concerned, you are quite prepared to admit even the most trivial documents into evidence. There are photographs that are marked with arrows by someone or that had previously been marked with arrows by someone, and these are things that I have never contested or challenged. I never challenged the idea that there was a crime in Ovcara and that should have been sufficient for you. That crime has been demonstrated before this court, before the courts in Belgrade so there is no doubt as to the existence of a crime there. But many Prosecution documents of a trivial nature have been admitted into evidence, and therefore I don't think that I'm being treated fairly. I won't suggest anything be admitted into evidence. I'll use documents in the course of my cross-examination. But as to what you admit into evidence or not, well, finally, that's not something that concerns me. Secondly, the Registry is very late with the translation of those documents. They haven't even translated documents that I submitted five months ago, and I'm no longer providing the Registry with new documents for translation. Those two large books has been extended until the beginning of the Defence case, or the translation of those two large books. I'm adapting to the situation. I'm not protesting. As far as Rule 92 ter is concerned, that Rule provides for the possibility of taking statements outside the framework of a trial or hearing. Rule 71 provides for the way in which such statements should be taken, a statement of any witness, if it is to be admitted into evidence -- well, such a statement should be taken by the Prosecution in my presence or in the presence of a member of my legal team. And as such, a document can be admitted into evidence. The legal nature of statements taken by the Prosecution outside the framework of the courtroom and without the presence of a member of the Defence team is such that such statements can be part of the indictment, but not part of the evidence. Everything noted or drafted by the Prosecution as part of the indictment or of something that supports the indictment, not evidence. Evidence must be something objectively obtained with regard to the purpose and intentions of the Prosecution. The Prosecution cannot present evidence, and here the current practice is for the Prosecution to present evidence by taking such statements and by suggesting that they be admitted into evidence and also by putting forward members of its own team as experts in this case. In certain other cases, the Prosecution investigators would appear, and before the Judges in the courtroom they would summarise the testimony of a large number of witnesses, and that was a procedure followed in some cases. The investigator took statements for about 20 witnesses who were victims and then compiled a statement of his own, a summary. And in certain cases, the Prosecution called such investigators to testify, instead of calling the 20 victims, the 20 witnesses. They will call, in such cases, their own investigator, who tells you about the experiences of the victims, and this is not something that can be accepted, in legal terms. This will go down in the history of international law, I'm quite persuaded of the fact, and I don't want to adapt myself to such a procedure. You should bring 92 ter in line with Rule 71, because there's a confrontation here between 92 ter and the main rules as laid out in Rule 71. Not a single Trial Chamber has tried to resolve the problems of that conflict between those two Rules because of the corrupted or incompetent lawyers who work here. Proceed as you wish. In one specific case, I asked you to re-examine your decision. If you refuse to do so, I'll adapt to that, and that's it, but I will not cooperate in this procedure that is contrary to the law. It's contrary to the law to have such provisions in the Rules and to include previous statements of witnesses, statements drafted by the Prosecution. The Prosecution also confirms that they drafted such statements. There's no doubt about this. This is something that has been compiled by the Prosecution. The Prosecution knows that the witness is not capable of telling the story in an identical manner here in the courtroom. The last witness, we had a notorious criminal and quite obviously a liar. Well, in his case, the Prosecution wrote a statement for him, and the witness, who was prepared to lie all the time, could not remember all of his incredible lies. He wasn't able to repeat those lies in the courtroom. I reminded him of the lies that he forgot to mention or didn't have time to mention, because it's more difficult to remember lies than facts, it's easier to forget lies. Someone who lies a lot will trip up on his own lies, whereas facts leave indelible traces in one's mind until the end of one's life. And when witnesses who are victims are concerned, that's even more so the case. When someone starts manipulating with the tragedy of certain victims, well, this is quite simply a new crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber will deliberate on the matter to see whether we stand by our previous decision or modify it, in light of what you have said and in light of what Mr. Mundis has told us. So we shall now show the videos up until 10.30, last week's videos. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps before or while we get these videos ready to go, I do have two other very short matters that I'd like to raise. The first one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is another issue which I wanted to address and which I didn't because Mr. Seselj wanted to take the floor, so I shall give you the floor, Mr. Mundis, in a few moments, but I would like to ask the Registrar to move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just two very brief matters to raise before we commence with the videotapes. The first concerns a list that was provided to the Registry for transmission to the accused yesterday. This is the list that follows from our discussion, I believe it was on the 20th of March, in which we indicated we would make a list of all videos in the Prosecution's possession available to the accused so that he could review that list. I wanted to indicate that a list was provided. I'm not sure if it was handed to the accused yesterday or perhaps this morning or later today, but we have provided him with a 979-page spreadsheet in English, which he agreed to accept at the earlier hearing, and I did want to follow up with the Trial Chamber on that because I informed you that I would be notifying you when that lift was made available. So the accused either has or will have shortly a list of -- a 979-page list of videos in the Prosecution's possession with a tick box for him to indicate which videotapes he would like and we will endeavour to disclose those to the accused. The second point, Your Honours: Yesterday afternoon, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking leave to amend its 65 ter exhibit list to include a booklet we've produced of insignia and uniforms worn by certain armed formations and military units during the conflict 1991 to 1995. Attached to that motion was a DVD containing an electronic version of this booklet. I do have about six copies of that book here in the courtroom today, and if it would be helpful, I can distribute those to the Trial Chamber, legal officer, and the accused at this point in time. Perhaps if I could have the assistance of the usher, we could distribute these books. I will also indicate, for the benefit of Dr. Seselj, that the translation of the first couple of pages of this book is -- into the Serbian language is forthcoming. Other than that, everything, I believe, is self-explanatory in the booklet. But the cover page and the first page are two that require translation, is in the process of being done, and will be disclosed as soon as that's available. And, again, I simply wanted to prepare or produce for the Chamber a hard copy of this book. It is the subject, as I indicated, of a motion to add to our exhibit list, and that was filed yesterday afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Mundis. The Trial Chamber will, of course, examine this book, which is made up of photographs of soldiers and various insignia, which will help us better understand these insignia which are mentioned. On page 109, for instance, the White Eagles, we can see the insignia here fairly well. Two eagles are shown. The Assault Battalion of the White Eagles. This could be extremely interesting. Mr. Seselj, of course, will give us his comments, if he has any, on the insignia in question. If need be, this booklet will be given an exhibit number, but only once Mr. Seselj has told us whether he is in favour or against, and if he's opposed to it, for what reasons. But take your time, Mr. Seselj. We are not going to be asking you today to take a stand on this. But if you tell us right away that you agree, then we can give this booklet an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I've already had a look at the document. This can be dealt with immediately. I know everything about the document, and I think it's impossible to have this document admitted into evidence because we don't know who the author of the document is. This isn't stated anywhere in the document. I don't know whether this book was published somewhere or not, or did members of the Prosecution compile this on the basis of their own criteria? No explanation is provided. This isn't a book in any sense of the term. It's only a book in that someone compiled something in this way. It's a handmade book. It can't admitted into evidence. We don't know when this was drafted. We'd need an expert report to accompany this. And as I had a look at this immediately, from page 78, the insignia of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, have a look at page 79, this was never the insignia used by volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party, nor was it the official flag of the Serbian Radical Party or its section of the Serbian Chetnik Movement. We never produced a flag of this kind, never, and the Serbian Chetnik Movement didn't have any particular insignia that distinguished it from the Serbian Radical Party. The Serbian Radical Party has one symbol, and that symbol is used for all the party -- for the entire party and all its sections. So page 79, what we have on 79, is invented. Such flags were the handmade products of individuals, of certain enthusiasts, certain individuals who had fallen in love with the Chetnik traditions, so we didn't believe that old Chetnik traditions needed such symbols. On page 80, this is the flag of the Serbian Radical Party. It's been visually modified to a certain extent here, but on the whole that's the flag. Page 81, this flag and emblem have nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party, nor did the Serbian Radical Party ever produce anything of this kind. This has been produced by someone on an independent basis. It's handmade work. There's not a single company in Serbia that is involved in producing flags, symbols, badges, and that produced these items in a serial manner. Page 82, similarly, this has been nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. The Serbian Radical Party never produced items of this kind, and our members never had such emblems on them. On page 83, this is an emblem that again is a handmade emblem. It does say "The Serbian Chetnik Movement" on it, that's true, but this was never the official emblem used by the Serbian Chetnik Movement. There was a section within the Serbian Radical Party, that was a branch of the Serbian Radical Party. Perhaps it was an independent Chetnik movement. Such movements appeared in various places. On page 84, again this emblem says "The Serbian Chetnik Movement," but we don't know who produced this or when, and it has nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. Again we're talking about someone's handiwork here. On page 85 it says "The Main Staff of the Serbian Chetnik Movement." It has absolutely nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. The Serbian Radical Party never had items of this kind, nor did it produce or distribute such items. On page 86, it's one of the modified versions of the old cockade Chetnik caps. Someone produced these items as souvenirs and sold them in the street. This was never officially accepted by the Serbian Radical Party. And then if we carry on and have a look at page 87, we can see that it has to do with the Ravno Gora Serbian Chetniks. Well, these Chetniks never had such official insignia. This is someone's handiwork. Again, the Prosecution has to compile a list of the various Chetnik organisations in existence in Serbia, Montenegro, at Republika Srpska, and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, they had to break it down on the base of these various organisations. On page 88, yet again this is a -- is some produce of symbols that was sold at street stalls. This wasn't legally produced, it wasn't legally sold. This was sold from cardboard boxes in the streets of Belgrade. On page 89, well, look, this emblem contains the Serbian flag, the skull, crossed swords, and it says "Freedom or Death." That's a Chetnik slogan that's one century old, but it has absolutely nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. It doesn't say the Serbian Radical Party. It doesn't say the Serbian Chetnik Movement, either. On page 90, the Sarajevo Chetnik Detachment, well, that's the detachment that later joined the Army of Republika Srpska. It was the 2nd Company of a certain battalion within a certain brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska and it has nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. On page 91, you can see it again, a cap with a cockade or kind of cockade cap. What does this have to do with the Serbian Radical Party? The Serbian Radical Party cannot appropriate a traditional Serbian cap or Subara. On page 92, we have the traditional Serbian "sajkaca" cap with a cockade cap. What does this have to do with the Serbian Radical Party? We can't appropriate such items because this is the heritage of the entire Serbian people. On page 93, you can see a group of individuals, two of whom have beards, and one of them has the flag -- or a flag with Chetnik symbols. Where's the proof that this has anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party? One of them is wearing a Montenegrin cap. It's the second one. On page 94, again you can see a group of soldiers. This is a photograph we've already seen in the courtroom, and one of the soldiers is wearing a Subara cap and a kind of -- a version of the cockade cap. We can't see what version is at stake. What does this have to do with the Serbian Radical Party again? Sir, on page 95, 96, and 97, on those pages you can see two versions of the insignia of the Special Manda Unit in Bilek [phoen]. This one individual became a member of the Serbian Radical Party. I did declare that he was a Chetnik Vojvoda, but the Serbian Radical Party didn't form his unit, and his unit wasn't formed of volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party it sent to the unit from Serbia. Mitar Maksimovic, Manda, subsequently joined the Serbian Radical Party. He was a member of ours, later he was the president of the municipality in Bilek, the people elected him, Mr. President, and then five or six years ago he died in a traffic accident. So none of this can be tied to the Serbian Radical Party, apart from the flag on page 80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have made your comments. Mr. Mundis, first we'd like to know who made this document. I assume that it is the OTP. The second observation, we would like to know where these insignias come from, which witness brought them. We know nothing of this. There are insignias that don't request any comments. The one on page 5, JNA insignia, I believe this will not be challenged. As to the TOs, well, Mr. Seselj now is challenging a good number of insignias, starting with number 80 and so on and so forth, as of page 78. All this is under SRS volunteers or SCP volunteers, and he is challenging all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the photo book indeed was compiled by the Office of the Prosecutor based on a large number of sources. Many of those insignia are simply -- or uniforms are simply photographs that are in our possession. The information comes from a wide variety of sources. There's not one witness who provided us with the photos, or pictures, or actual uniform insignia themselves. Let me just put on the record and make it very clear the purpose of this book. It doesn't serve any independent purpose or function. The usefulness of such a tool is to assist the Trial Chamber in those situations where we have a live witness come in and testify about what he saw on someone's uniform, and in that sense the proper recourse for the accused is to cross-examine the witness. For example, we bring in a witness who says, "I saw a soldier wearing a uniform with insignia on it. It looks to me or to the best of my recollection it was the patch on page 112." If the accused thinks that that patch on page 112 is a bogus patch or something that was made up or something that we created, he can cross-examine the witness on that. It's simply a tool to allow us to visualise the various insignia that witnesses might indicate in the courtroom here during their testimony that a person was wearing. The book serves no value whatsoever in the course of the witness testimony, and the proper recourse for the accused would be to cross-examine the witness who says, "I saw a someone wearing a uniform or an insignia that looks just like the one on page 7 or page 12 or page 96." So it's not some sort of expert compilation booklet that we'll be relying on in the absence of any witness testimony, so I think that to a certain extent it's a bit of much a do about nothing. The book serves no purpose unless and until a witness comes in and says, "This is the uniform I saw someone wearing on the day of this attack," and the accused can cross-examine on that point, the Trial Chamber can ask questions on that point. The book, sitting on a shelf by itself, serves no purpose whatsoever without witness testimony to identify the various patches or insignia. I would also guess during the course of this trial that a large number of those pages in that booklet probably won't be identified by anyone, but we simply put together a compilation of material gathered by this office over the course of many years concerning uniforms and insignia, and there's nothing secret about that. It's simply something that would assist the Trial Chamber again in visualising material that -- that would be helpful to the Trial Chamber in terms of identifying uniforms, units, insignia, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the insignia on page 80, the insignia of the Serbian Radical Party, you're not contesting this one, are you, two eagles, "Serbian Radical Party" on a blue background?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a strangely-deformed flag of the Serbian Radical Party. The eagle is elongated. The letters are too close together. The original Serbian Radical Party flag has an eagle which is not elongated in this way. And the spacing between the letters is greater. The letters are in a semicircle. Here somebody intentionally wanted the letters to form the letter U, which has an extremely negative meaning in the Serbian national consciousness because it is reminiscent of the Ustasha in World War II. We would never have done something like this. If it's a semicircle, then it's the flag of the Serbian Radical Party. So this is an intentionally-distorted flag of the Serbian Radical Party, in my opinion. However, I wish to draw your attention to something else, Judge. This is something put together in haste. It's not the result of systematic research. It's simply a compilation of things the OTP has come across over a number of years. It might have a certain value in the proceedings. For example, had I had this available when the two Muslim protected witnesses were testifying, and one of them mentioned some sort of Seselj assault units, you remember how I challenged this. I had never heard of assault units. And on page 111, we have a symbol "White Eagles Assault Battalion." Had I had this at the time, I might have shown this to the witness and said, "Did these assault troops which were allegedly mine wear this sort of insignia?" And had the witness confirmed this, this would have proved my point. However, the form has not been met for this to qualify as evidence, because the OTP cannot produce evidence. We can be grateful to the Prosecutor, because we have now discovered that the OTP is the author of this book, because it provided us with material that we can use with more or less success.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, given Mr. Seselj's objection, we will not give a number to this book. But if a witness says, "I saw an insignia," that the OTP can show him the book at such-and-such a page, and say, "Yes, this is what I saw," "This is not what I saw," and through this means we will be able to obtain information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I want to say that we will not give a number -- will not admit this document because the Prosecution so far has not tendered this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Lattanzi. Yes, at this point, Your Honours, all we're asking is that we be allowed to add it to the exhibit list. We're not simply tendering it. And, of course, to reiterate, in light of the accused's last comments, this book is not evidence until a witness or witnesses come in and start pointing to various pages or describing material on various pages of the book, at which point in time we will, in fact, tender the book into evidence, or at least those pages of it that a witness has identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So in the first step, you're just asking for this document to be added to the exhibit list, and whenever witnesses come and recognise such-and-such insignia, you will tender the page in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think everyone understood. It's 10.20. I think we should have a 20-minute break, and then we will resume with the videos, since we will have checked all administrative and technical problems. Another topic, Mr. Mundis, first?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, it would be very helpful perhaps after the break if we could get a ruling from the Trial Chamber as to the reconsideration on the 92 ter issue. That, of course, affects our planning in terms of how we discuss with the witness who is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll consult on this immediately. We're going to study it and deliberate over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber will issue its decision on whether or not we will apply Rule 92 ter for Witness VS-1014. The Trial Chamber deliberated and maintains its former position, the position of February 27th, 2008. Therefore, the OTP will tender the written statement and will ask the normal questions to the witness in order to confirm the entirety of the written statement. The Prosecutor will show a number of documents. I don't believe that there's many, I think there's only two. After this, the Trial Chamber will put questions to the witness so that the witness gives explanations on a few points in his written statement. Then the Trial Chamber will give the floor to Mr. Seselj, asking him if he wants to cross-examine the witness. If he does not want to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Seselj will still have the possibility of tendering the statement made to BiH authorities which he believes contradicts the written statement, and later on, when examining the written statement, the answers given by the witness to the Chamber is put, and after having possibly looked at the statement made to the authorities of the BiH, that the Trial Chamber will decide whether the written statement will be admitted or not. This is the ruling, and the Prosecution can now prepare for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will put on the record, as I indicated earlier, that it is almost certain, if not very likely, that in the event Mr. Seselj declines to cross-examine the witness and then seeks to tender a prior statement of the witness, that the Prosecution will be vehemently opposed to that. Our view would be that he has the opportunity to cross-examine the witness on the prior statement, and if he foregoes that, then our view will be that he should be precluded from tendering that statement. I simply indicate that now so that the accused is very well aware of the position we will be taking with respect to any prior statements of the witness. Having said that, Mr. President, we are ready to commence with the next chapter, if you will, or category of videos. These concern instigation, hate speech, and propaganda. The first clip bears 65 ter number 6002B. This document -- or video was received around the 18th of August, 1999, from an unknown source. This again is amateur footage of a speech by the accused. This clip runs for several minutes. This is 65 ter number 6002B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "What represents our most vulnerable point, the Kosovo-Metohija issue, the issue of the Albanian separatist insurgent. The current military police action in Kosovo-Metohija succeeded in eliminating the most extreme aspects of Albanian separatism and repression of the Serbian population that lives there, but I'm convinced that a lasting solution cannot be achieved in this way. In order to achieve a solution to the Kosovo and Metohija question, I propose a new colonization of Kosovo and Metohija. "The question now is how. Of course, one should have no illusions about the possibility of returning those Serbs who have left Kosovo and Metohija, who have learned what it means to live with Albanians, a primitive and uncivilised people, as their next-door neighbours, who have reached Belgrade and Serbia proper, the possibility of returning them to the -- they have found jobs, they send children to school. A possibility of returning them to the nightmare of Kosovo and Metohija, it would be inhumane of any regime to force them by any political means to go back. But the fact that the Serbs who had fled Kosovo and Metohija for the most part would not come back to Kosovo and Metohija does not mean that there can be no new colonization. In order to carry out a new colonization of Kosovo and Metohija, I propose that the Yugoslav and Serbian capital be moved to the area of Kosovo and Metohija. "Whether it is moved to Pristina, Prizren, or some other place is not so important. What is important is that by moving the capital, the state institutions would be moved, all the state bodies and institutions, several hundred thousand government employees, the civil servants and members of their families would be moved. In this way, the overall ethnic composition of the population of Kosovo and Metohija would change in a significant way, and it would mean a fresh financial injection, and the economic development of this depressed region would accelerate. Of course, I propose that all the military and police academies not directly linked to the commands of particular military districts also be moved to the region of Kosovo and Metohija, which means that several thousand commissioned and non-commissioned officers and police officials and their family members would move, which would also impact the overall ethnic composition of the population of Kosovo and Metohija. "Further, I propose that any economic assistance to Kosovo and Metohija, that is, to the Albanian population that lives there, be immediately stopped. According to the data published by the regime-backed media in Belgrade sometime in March of this year, Kosovo and Metohija receives a million dollars a day from the so-called assistance fund for underdeveloped republics and regions, and what this does for the most part is subsidize the outsized Albanian birth rate. I have nothing against the Albanians continuing to multiply as fast as they do, but not at the expense of Serbs. We, the Serbs, will not finance their disproportionate birth rate. "If they want to procreate at this rate, they should themselves support their children or face the fact that their children will starve. We, the Serbs, will no longer finance them. Since it has become evident that Albania, as a state, has taken a staunchly hostile position towards Yugoslavia and Serbia, and since it has become evident that the vast majority of members of the Albanian ethnic minority living within our borders are staunchly hostile towards the Serbian and Yugoslav state sovereignty and territorial integrity, especially in this vital part of our country, I believe that Yugoslavia and Serbia states have all the authority based on the international law to do anything in their power to protect our state sovereignty and territorial integrity. In that sense, I propose that a zone of 50 or perhaps even 100 kilometres along the Albanians border be declared a zone of strategic interest for our country. "That the entire Albanian population be moved out of this zone, with just monetary compensation, and be directed to resettle themselves elsewhere in other parts of Yugoslavia, I repeat, with a just compensation, to resettle, let us say, in the territory of the present-day Croatia and Slovenia because they are the most developed. Because these are the most developed parts of Yugoslavia, they would have the least problem in absorbing them, giving them jobs, securing them for civil protection, and it turns out that the Croats and the Slovenes like them the most, support them the most. I am convinced that they will enthusiastically accept this proposal of mine. "By presenting this proposal, I am taking into account the indisputable fact that the real centre of the Albanian separatist insurgence is neither Pristina nor Tirana but Zagreb, and the arable land in this zone along the Albanian border could temporarily be placed under military management. The army would establish agricultural farms, organise agricultural production. This is the most fertile land in all of Europe which under the current Albanian management is yielding the lowest crops in all of Europe because the Albanians are used to living off the assistance of the rest of Yugoslavia and have no need to work or farm this land efficiently. "Military management of several years, let us say 10 or 15 years, would significantly contribute to the country recovering from its economic crisis, especially the bread basket of Metohija could feed almost all of Central Europe and to date cannot even feed Kosovo and Metohija. And what I consider the most important at this time, the most important point, I propose that all 360.000 Albanian immigrants who have crossed into Serbia and Yugoslavia from Albania since the 6th of April, 1941, urgently be sent back to Albania, that they be delivered to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees. Throughout the world there are so many richer and larger countries, so let them take them, let them show a little of their humanity. Why should we, the Serbs, always prove our humanity and be stabbed in the back by these Albanian immigrants?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, do you have any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even today, I am very proud of this speech of mine made in 1989. I regret that the OTP did not play the entire speech. I wish that in 1989, I had had an opportunity to come to power. However, there are several problems here. First of all, the dating of this speech is incorrect. It can't have been on the 8th of August, 1989. It can only have been towards the end of August or in early September 1989. Secondly, the question arises as to the temporal relevance. The speech was made in 1989, and my indictment covers the period from the 1st of August, 1991, to September 1993. A third issue is also one of relevance. Kosovo and Metohija and the events there are not, unfortunately, covered by the indictment against me. The question then arises of the motives of the OTP in tendering this document. Fourthly, one must bear in mind that the year 1989 was still a year of full communist dictatorship in Serbia and Yugoslavia. There was no multi-party system. In 1989, I was still a dissident, I was still being persecuted, and I was making speeches and giving lectures as an individual. When I left prison in 1986, until the spring of 1989, I couldn't even travel abroad. The right to a passport was denied me. After a battle of three years, after a judgement of the highest court in Yugoslavia, I was granted a passport, and that was the first time I was able to travel abroad after many, many years. All this has to be borne in mind, and yet the OTP is unable to explain why they wish to tender this speech. As the OTP cannot provide a single argument to induce the Trial Chamber to admit this document, I support the admission of this document so the Trial Chamber can do this without entering into all these objections. I do want this speech to be admitted because I am proud of it. However, what I say about relevance remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This speech was held in 1989, end of August or beginning of September. You specify that it's the 8th of August, but this is challenged. The second point, this has to do with Kosovo. Nobody challenges that Kosovo is not part of the indictment, which the accused regrets. This is what he's just told us and has told us on several occasions. The accused is telling us that in 1989, former Yugoslavia was operating as such and he was a dissident. This document can be useful in what way, even though the accused is not against the admission of this document, but what is the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it can go to evidence of state of mind, the accused's thoughts and processes with respect to other matters that are relevant in the indictment. We could certainly set forth a number of additional arguments if Your Honours would like to hear that. Our view would be that because the accused does not object to the document or the video going into evidence, that that really should be taken into consideration by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall ask my colleagues what they think about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bench, after having deliberated on the matter for some time, has decided to admit the document and ask the Registrar to give it an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to specify, because it's not mentioned in the English version, this decision was a majority decision. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next video clip bears 65 ter number 6015A. This video is from May 1991. It runs a little bit longer than one minute. It originally was from TV Novi Sad, a programme entitled "Without Incisions and Without Anaesthesia." The Office of the Prosecutor received this from AID in Sarajevo on 27 August 1998. Again, this video bears 65 ter number 6015A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "What do you see as the outcome? Should this thing now started be continued in the sense -- "My opinion is that the army must disarm the Ustashas urgently, and then we will recall the Chetniks, bring them all back and disarm them, if the army does this. If the army doesn't do this, and there's no more time for waiting, now we will set about disarming the Croats ourselves. We sent units into Zagreb itself and into many other Croatian towns, special groups equipped and trained for sabotage and terrorist operations. "If the Croats mistreat the Serbian people in those areas where we can't protect the Serbs, if they carry out genocide against them, we will conduct reprisals in places where the Croats are weakest. And you know that when reprisals are carried out, when revenge is taken then revenge is blind and many innocent Croats will suffer. But what can you do? "While they still got time, they should think about the consequences, and let's hope they don't take the Ustasha dagger and hold it up with us carrying out reprisals. This is their last warning. If it ends up with us carrying out reprisals, we won't be held responsible for the consequences."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing against having this admitted into evidence, in principle, and I am proud of this statement, but there are a few comments I'd like to make. Firstly, the video is too short. It's one minute and five seconds' long, if I have calculated the time correctly. It's too brief an extract from a lengthier discussion that took an hour and a half, if my memory serves me well. Secondly, the issue of relevance occurs. This is a video from May 1991. This is outside the time frame of the indictment, and we should bear in mind the framework in which this was done. In May 1991, the Serbian Radical Party was a small, extra-parliamentary party. It didn't have a single member in the people's assembly. It was only registered in March 1991, and we had our first member of Parliament in June of that year, and we only had one representative until the end of 1992. This should be borne in mind. It's important. And, secondly, shortening a video in this manner is tantamount to massacring it, because naturally we're dealing with a warning here, don't do certain things, cease attacking, don't incite revenge. Everything that was said was said as a warning, as a deterrent. You should bear in mind the period when this was done. It was in May, that period when we were sending volunteers to certain villages in Slavonia. We wanted to withdraw the volunteers. We were prepared to do this if the army disarmed the Ustasha. And all of this was said in these several sentences. If we had seen a lengthier extract from this video, it would have all been a lot clearer. This isn't a hate speech. It's a warning. It says, "Don't take up arms. Revenge is blind. The innocent will suffer," and so on and so forth. So the sense is, in fact, quite the opposite of the sense that the Prosecution intends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a speech aimed as a deterrent, not a hate speech. This is what you have just imparted to us just now. You complain about the fact that it is an excerpt of an interview which lasted one hour and 30 minutes, but we look into the relevance here, because this was dated the 22nd of May, 1991. No MP was represented at the time, so there is no objection as a matter of principle. The Trial Chamber has factored in your remarks, and we'll give it an exhibit number. Let me say that this was shown very quickly. You were wearing a Blazer, and on the Blazer there was an insignia there was an insignia which we cannot distinguish very clearly, in fact we can't see it at all but you were wearing an insignia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I suggest that we have a look at the video again, and we could zoom in on that insignia. That's technically possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see the video again just for one minute. We have time to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Seemingly, there is an insignia where the heart is, but we can't see it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. We can't see it, so we're having a hard time. Mr. Seselj, either you were wearing an insignia or you weren't. The image is not self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot conclude that this is an insignia on the basis of this video. Perhaps it's a bullet hole. Perhaps someone shot me with a large-calibre bullet a little earlier. That's in the sphere of assumptions, but I'll tell you what the truth is. This was really the Serbian coat of arms, a golden coat of arms, the two-headed white eagle with a "Nemanjic" crown on it, surrounded by olive branches, and there was a cross, four Ss, four letters S, but this is something that I can tell you, although you can't see anything. I only wore such a coat of arms. I never wore a coat of arms with the skull on it. I respect that 100-year-old tradition, when Chetniks had such a coat of arms and such a flag, for certain reasons, but there's no longer any need to use such an emblem because it's a pirate symbol in the West, and anyone in the West who sees such a symbol believes that it's a matter of pirates. We didn't want to be seen as pirates, and that's why we avoided such emblems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, is this coat of arms in our booklet or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This emblem is the coat of arms of Serbia today. It's on the Serbian flag, if you have a look, and I can have a look or go through the document that we've been provided with. It will take me a minute or two, if it's -- have a look at page 32. You don't have to have a look at the frame that the two-headed eagle is in, but just have a look at the two-headed white eagle with the crown on its head, and you'll see that this is the coat of arms that I was wearing on that day in the video. But don't pay attention to the frame, because the Army of Republika Srpska constructed the frame for other reasons. So if you don't pay attention to the frame, this is the traditional Serbian coat of arms, and it goes back to the Nemanjic era and the Middle Ages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, having specified this, can I just ask whether the crown is still a part of the coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The crown is part of the state Serbian coat of arms. The crown symbolizes statehood, imperial statehood. Serbia was an empire, had two empires, the emperors, Emperor Dusan and another emperor. So this is the case for the coat of arms now, but it's not on flag of the Serbian Radical Party. The coat of arms on the flag doesn't have a crown, you just have the two-headed white eagle and the two crossed swords. How did this emblem of the Serbian Radical Party appear? We had in mind the Chetnik emblem. The Chetnik emblem doesn't have a crown. It's a two-headed eagle with crossed swords, but it has a skull. That's the old tradition. When we constructed -- when we made the coat of arms for the Serbian Radical Party, we didn't use the skull. The skull is never used as an emblem for the Serbian Radical Party. We had the four Ss and the cross and the shield, but we maintained the crossed swords. It's a modified old Chetnik symbol. It's not a state symbol. It's been adapted to the ideology of the current Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having specified this. This is useful. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number for the video, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next video clip bears 65 ter number 6016A. This video is from 4 May 1991. It's a video compilation of television broadcasts from 4 to 6 May 1991, originating from SFRY TV, submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor by Natasha Kandic on 1 April 1996. This again is 65 ter number 6016A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "All those who proclaimed our honourable duke, "Red Duke," using skilful deceits and their servants in the media should just take one look at the other side of the Danube River, and they will see how much effort our Dr. Vojislav Seselj invested in the last month in helping the Serbs of Slavonia Baranja, and the Serbian Krajina. In the last months, helping the Serbs of Slavonia, Baranja and Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it looks like the Prosecution overcame its timidity and now it says that Natasha Kandic is the source from which they obtained this video. This is a positive development, as far as the conduct of the Prosecution is concerned, although I saw that he blushed somewhat when he mentioned the name "Natasha Kandic," but that doesn't matter now. It's important to know the circumstances under which this video was shot. It was on the 4th of May, 1991. The Prosecution has only taken a short extract out of the video that concerns Mirko Jovic, a guest of the Serbian Radical Party. This was a short extract. It was after the large victory of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party on Borovo village on the 2nd of May. 16 Croatian policemen died on that occasion, according to our information many more, because the Croats never listed all their victims, all their losses. This is a protest meeting in front of Tito's grave in Belgrade. It was called "Assault on the House of Flowers." And when we convened this meeting, there was a state of emergency in the JNA Main Staff. Tito's grave was being guarded, and Veselin Sljivancanin was the commander of the unit who had organised machine-gun nests to mow us down if we really ran towards the grave, so we mocked the grave of Tito and we had a huge stake. We wanted to show how we intended to deal with the vampire Tito. So this meeting has a very particular connotation. This could be evidence for the Defence, this video. You should have seen my speech at the meeting. I said how the Main Staff had convened, how they said that they would open fire if we approached Tito's grave, et cetera. But Veselin Sljivancanin told me that they had already organised machine-gun nests around Tito's grave, and they would have opened fire if we'd really started running towards the grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we shall give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P351.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next video bears 65 ter number 6016B. This tape also originates from SFRY TV. It was also submitted by Natasha Kandic on 1 April 1996. It's a clip from the same video compilation as the prior video clip. This clip runs approximately one and a half minutes' long. It was originally taken in early May 1991. 65 ter number 6016B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We are not playing around and the Ustasha leader Franjo Tudjman is now finally aware that we are not playing around. We are going to realise everything that we defined as our political goals, and we are guaranteeing this with our own lives. Not even the Turkish Empire could disgrace the Serbian people, nor the Austro-Hungarian Empire, nor fascist Germany. So what could that pitiful bunch of non-historical Croats do? They are attacking unarmed people. They have beaten up dozens of Serbian young men in the police stations. They are attacking women and children, while the Serbian fighters for freedom are only attacking the armed Ustashas. There is not a single unarmed Croat that was attacked by the Serbs. There is not a single Croatian woman or Croatian child that could point their finger at a Serb. We will do away with all armed Croats who are attacking Serbian villages. Not one will survive."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My first comment concerning Mr. Mundis's statement. He said that the SFRY TV produced this video. Perhaps Yutel was behind it. They were under the control of the then Prime Minister Ante Markovic, but that should then be stated. And this video is of the same meeting, and so then one extract would be better. And, thirdly, this is obviously exculpatory material, because I quite directly state that our position is that we will never oppress the Croatians, the civilians, women and children. I said they would never be the victims of our volunteers. I said that only armed Croats attacking Serbian villages would be targeted. In my opinion, this is material of an exculpatory nature, but since the Prosecution is tendering it, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number, please, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 6017A. This clip also runs approximately one and a half minutes' long. It was submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor on or about 1 January 2001, from an unknown source. The approximate date of the video clip is 6 May 1991, and this again is 65 ter number 6017A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Our Western enemies are attempting to carry out a new genocide against the Serbian people. Brothers and sister Serbs, it is our task to stop it, and we are sending this message to our enemies: Not only shall we avenge the present victims, but we will avenge the previous ones, too, when they dared to put the Ustasha knife under the Serbian throat again. Bosnia and the brave Serbian Herzegovina, it is particularly you who must not allow to be divided. You have one political party, the Serbian Democratic Party. You have your leadership, which has proved its qualities in action on the front lines and which has upheld the honour of Serbdom. They showed the Ustasha, who are superior in manpower, that the Serbian heroism is still alive. The Serbian Chetnik units will be active in all other areas of Western Serbia, in Serbian Krajina, in Serbian Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. We shall not give up a single inch of Serbian territory. Let the Slovenes leave Yugoslavia. They have never been our brothers or friends. Let the Croats go too, let Croatia secede, but we are not giving them an inch of the territory to the east of the Karlobag -- of the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac line."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naturally, I'm proud of this speech of mine, too. It was on the 6th of May, on St. George’s day on Mount Romanija. I regret the fact that we've only seen a short extract. We should have had a look at the entire video. I appeared on horse back. It was in front of the cave of a well-known Serbian "hajduk," Starina Novak, from the period of the fighter against the Turks. But, again, the issue of relevance presents itself. This is the 6th of May, 1991, and the indictment covers the period from the 1st of August, 1991. Naturally, there's a short extract which gives a fall impression. We should have had a look at a lengthier extract. As far as the contents are concerned, there's nothing that poses a problem and this continues to be the policies pursued by the Serbian Radical Party. We radicals will never relinquish the western Serbian territories, and sooner or later we will free the Serbian territory under Croatia now. So there's nothing that's in dispute now. The Republic of Serbian Krajina has to be liberated sooner or later. As to when or how, well, that remains to be seen. Perhaps we won't carry this out, we who are alive today, but perhaps our children will. We'll never give this idea up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar, could we have a number for this clip?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip, Your Honours, bears 65 ter number 6019B. This is a video clip from November 1991, from a television programme called "NS Plus." This is the second of three videotapes connected to a collection of material from the Croatia Ministry of the Interior. The clip in question apparently was originally broadcast on TV Novi Sad, and this clip runs approximately two minutes. This is P6019B.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection before we have a look at the video. Perhaps the interpretation was mistaken. I was told it was from November. It can't be November. It was probably the 11th of May. That's what it says on paper. Perhaps the interpreter made a mistake or the Prosecution, but this doesn't go back to November. The date isn't November, as it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, it seems that this video dates back to May and not November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It should be May. If I said "November," then I misspoke, but it is from the 11th of May, 1991, as indicated on the table that was distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "There weren't many advertisements, so let's carry on. Ilija Srbin from Novi Sad: A decision was taken today by the Croatian Parliament that the Knin Krajina would fall in June. That was at 3.00 p.m. today.
