I wasn't listening, I don't know if you heard about it. What is your reaction to that decision? "Well, to be frank, I am personally looking forward to this Croatian attack. It seems that they weren't taught enough of a lessen in Borovo Selo, so we'll make sure that they're given a more severe lesson, then. "Has the Chetnik detachment already been formed in Bijeli Mani Staro [phoen], when will it be ready? "Yes, there is the committee of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, the committee of the Serbian Radical Party for Baranja, and there are a lot of Chetniks. "Dragan Jandric from Futogo [phoen] would like to hear what you have to say about the statement you made to Pogledi, 'I'll arrest Tudjman, and what kind of guns can hit the letter U on the heads of members of the Croatian MUP from a distance of 1.500 metres.' "I said that I would arrest Tudjman, Mesic and Ante Markovic before they arrested me. A warrant for my arrest has been issued in Croatia as well as in Bosnia-Herzegovina. But it doesn't worry me very much. I never travel in Croatia, anyway, I travel in Serbian lines, in Serbian Krajina, Serbian Slavonia, Serbian Baranja, and Serbian Western Srem. Serbian Chetniks have very good guns these days. It is true that they have a lot of old Thompsons made in 1942, but they have proved to be very effective. You know, if a Chetnik is a good shot and hits the Croat in the forehead, it makes the Croat's eyes pop out, or if a burst of fire cuts a Croat across the neck, his head is literally severed from the body. The gun are very good. Naturally, we only shoot at armed Croats attacking Serbian villages. We have never shot at an unarmed Croat."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm surprised this is exculpatory material. I just correct something. We're not talking about rifles. We're talking about the Thompson automatic. It has a large calibre. I can't remember the calibre exactly, perhaps 45. I can't remember exactly, but this calibre really leaves significant consequences wherever it hits a man, in the head or in the chest. The journalist was wrong. The Thompson doesn't have a range of 1.500 metres. Perhaps that's a range that's possible for the bullet, but the effective range is several hundred metres. This weapon is used for close-range combat. I just had to point this out. So it's a Thompson submachine-gun, and naturally there's nothing I change with regard to what I said here. But you can draw the conclusion that at almost every speech, I emphasise the fact that we are fighting against those and only those who attack Serbian villages and the Serbian people with their arms, but I never advocate attacking civilians, women and children, and this is always present in all my speeches. This is a basis that you can see in all my speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar, could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P354.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 6010A. This clip is from September 1991. The clip runs for approximately 18 seconds. This was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 6 November 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We will no longer forgive, like we did after the First and the Second World War. The time has come for us to square old accounts as well. The time has come for us to avenge all Serb victims and unite all Serb lands."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, it's incorrect that this was filmed in September 1991. It has to come from an earlier period, because this was the funeral of the first volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party who was killed, Gradimir Pesic. He was killed somewhere between Borovo Selo and Borovo Naselje in eastern Slavonia. The funeral was held in a village near Crna Trava in the south of present day Serbia. You will see that at that funeral, I'm wearing a short-sleeved shirt, which means that had to be really hot, it had to be summer, so it would have had to be before September 1991. The OTP had the whole speech held at the funeral. It was published in "Velika Serbia," The Gazette of the Serbian Radical Party, and it would have been better had they played the entire speech. Secondly, there's something really amazing here. It says that the recipient, Mr. Ulrich Mussemeyer, he is the recipient and he is the one submitting this, so I wish to learn from him how he handed over this clip over to himself. There has to be a source somewhere. This could have been filmed by Belgrade Television and played on the news. It could have been broadcast on the news, so RTS might be the source, Radio Television Serbia, or it may be some other source. I don't know who precisely filmed this, but you can't have Mr. Mussemeyer listed here both as the source and the recipient. Secondly, the OTP has the clip of my election speech in December 1991 during the election campaign. There, I explain in detail what is meant by punishing the Croats for the crimes of World War II. I explained there that it doesn't mean we will take our revenge by killing Croats. I say that we, the Serbs, are a chivalrous people. The Croats have to be punished in the way that people are punished in the modern world. They are punished for their genocide and their crimes by loss of territory. Just as Germany lost vast territories after World War II, so Croatia should have been punished and reduced to its realistic borders, the three counties of Zagreb, Krusevac, Varazdin. It's quite clear but the OTP doesn't wish to explain this here, so they play very brief clips in attempting to support in this way something that they cannot prove. The OTP has that footage in their archives, as it has a lot of other footage as well, but it did not -- it is not presenting these clips in a continuous manner. It's simply extracting small clips out of context, which can then be explained in a quite different manner from the way in which they could be explained if they were seen in the proper context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, in the document you seem to be the person who submits this video and also receives this video. Is this how it occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's true I got this video in I think it was 2001 -- just let me check this. No, it was in 2002, and I got it from the director of the Humanitarian Law Centre in Belgrade. I can give you also the name, if it's necessary, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now we have an explanation. Ms. Registrar -- Mr. Seselj first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very important for Mr. Mussemeyer to say the name. That's the most important issue here. Otherwise, it seems that he both sent it and received it. He should say who sent it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do you have the name of the director?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The name is Sanja [sic] Biserko.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to correct him. The name is Sonja Biserko, but I wanted to hear it live in the courtroom, because apart from Natasha Kandic, there's a whole menagerie of creatures doing similar work. Natasha Kandic is simply the one most visible in all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, we need a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit 355.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next videotape bears 65 ter number 6028A, this video clip coming from the Radio Television Belgrade is from the 18th of October, 1991. It was submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor by Natasha Kandic on 1 April 1996. The clip runs slightly less than one minute. This is 65 ter number 6028A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In the packed hall of the sports centre in Kosovska Mitrovica with the participation of its leader Vojislav Seselj, after playing the national anthem and after the introductory remarks, Vojislav Seselj addressed the audience. "A moment of decision. A fatal decision has arrived for the Serbian people. We have only two possible options to choose from: to accept the blackmail of the European community, the ultimatum of foreign charlatans to fall on our knees, and the other option is to put up a fight as men and to face all the challenges, to reject this ultimatum as the Serbs rejected the Austro-Hungarian ultimatum in 1914."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To this very day, I am proud of this speech of mine which I held in October of 1991. Just as then, various international tricksters were leading the European Union. Today, they are leading the European Union, and the enemy is the same. Even today, the European Union is taking away from us Kosovo and Metohija and blackmailing us, but we will not give in. We will not cooperate with our enemies from the European Union in the robbing of Serbia of Kosovo and Metohija. The Serbian enemies are mentioned here, our road forward cannot be towards Serbian enemies. But the question arises of the relevance of this to the indictment. The OTP should amend the indictment and say, for example, that I am opposed to the European Union. And indeed I am, because everything that it has done in the past 18 years has been to the detriment of the Serbian people. So this is really a political issue. Why is this not in my indictment? And the reason I'm being tried here is that I'm hostile to NATO, that I'm opposed to the USA, and that I'm a political opponent of the European Union. The OTP is demonstrating now that these are the real reasons why I'm on trial, but this should be put into the indictment. Why are they making up all sorts of crimes to put in the indictment when all of that is not true. It is true, however, that I am opposed to the European Union, that I'm opposed to the USA, and that I'm a vehement enemy of NATO. There's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We need a number for this video, Ms. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The final video clip to be shown today bears 65 ter number 6010B. This video is from the autumn of 1991. This clip runs for 40 seconds. I do note that the list indicates, under the description, this is clip B from this videotape. That is, in fact, an error. It should be clip C. This video excerpt comes from a documentary series entitled "Pictures of Words and Hate, Year 2," produced by the Foundation for the Right to Pictures and Words received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 6 November 2002. It was originally broadcast on TV Novi Sad, and this is 65 ter number 6010B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The Ustasha came to a Serbian village here, near Kukuruzari, and captured little Ilija, slaughtered him in front of his mother, and took him away like that. His mother is called Milica. This was on his birth. On his birthday -- his birthday, on the 2nd of August of this year, and his mother ran after them so they would at least give her her dead child back, but they didn't give her the child. They took him away and burned him later on. The only thing left of all this was the skull. She would not have even found the skull were it not for another woman, a Roman Catholic, albeit, but at least she had a measure of humanity of feeling in her, and she said, 'I know where they burned your child and I will tell you where the grave is.' So she went there, and all she could find was this skull."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, what is the relevance, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Propaganda, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you see how brazen The Hague Prosecutors Office is. To them, this is propaganda, when a Serbian priest is showing the skull of a young man slaughtered by the Ustasha, the Ustasha burned his body, and this, according to them, is propaganda. One should ask whether the OTP carried out an investigation to prove, by indisputable arguments, that this really is propaganda and not a realistic description of an actual event. This man is an eminent priest, today the bishop of Milosevski [phoen]. He has the honour of guarding the grave of St. Sava and very high-ranking -- he's one of the five most prominent priests of the Serbian Orthodox Church. And the Prosecutor simply says "propaganda." The question of relevance of course arises, relevance in this case, of such a clip, but this is exculpatory material because it shows what the other side was doing, and the OTP is omitting this. A false picture is being presented here in a calculated and tendentious manner. A false picture is being created in The Hague Tribunal of the events in the former Yugoslavia. This false picture is being created by the enormous huge numbers of Serbs who are accused and the very small number of others, Albanians, Macedonians and so on, who are accused. These others are being acquitted, such as Ramush Haradinaj, some Muslim generals who were acquitted here, and so on and so forth. And this is actually evidence against The Hague OTP, because in this war all sides committed crimes. I am not justifying any crime committed by the Serb side, and every crime has a perpetrator with a first and last name, the person who executed the crime and the person who ordered the crime. But the Croat and Muslim and Albanian sides were the first to start. They were the ones who started by committing crimes against the Serbs, and then some Serbs, out of blind revenge, committed other crimes. And of course I do not feel that this justifies those crimes, but it partly explains them, and it is brazen to show this clip, attributing Bishop Filaret to negative propaganda, whereas today they are affirming him as an honourable priest, an honourable man who at decisive moments stood up in the defence of the Serbian people and showed to the world what was being done to the Serbs. He opposed the Western propaganda which kept insisting that it was the Serbs who were the criminals, whereas the Croats, the Muslims and the Albanians were defenceless victims, which is why the Serbs were exposed to three months of cruel air strikes by NATO. I am grateful to the OTP for having committed this tactical error and broadcasting this clip, because it makes it possible for me to brand their intentions and their motives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will deliberate to see whether we admit it or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber has deliberated and decides to admit this video clip, which will be interpreted by the Trial Chamber in view of what has just been said. Could we please have a number, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P357.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That brings us to the end of the videos listed for today. The Prosecution has nothing further for today. We will make VS-1014 available tomorrow pursuant to Rule 92 ter and the Trial Chamber's earlier decisions concerning that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll ask my colleagues whether we should start at 8.30 or 9.00. It all depends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So tomorrow we will start at 8.30, because my colleagues have to sit in the afternoon, and so we will start tomorrow and the day after tomorrow at 8.30. The hearing is adjourned, and we will meet again -- well, I'll give you the floor in a minute, Mr. Seselj. But we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30. Mr. Seselj, what did you have to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that tomorrow the second witness announced for this week will not appear in the courtroom? It's very important. Should I prepare for him or not? If he won't appear tomorrow, let the Prosecutor confirm this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tomorrow, we have only one witness. The second one will only be there on Thursday? Is that it? For administrative reasons or another, he'll come on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. We have one witness for tomorrow, one witness for Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we resume tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of April, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.51 a.m.,
